span.label: exosomes - A CLASS THIS PAPER DEFINES TWICE, ONCE BY THE ROUTE A VESICLE TOOK AND ONCE BY ITS SIZE AND MARKERS, and the two definitions do not pick out the same things
span.quote: Exosomes are nano-sized biovesicles released into surrounding body fluids upon fusion of multivesicular bodies and the plasma membrane.

span.label: what is known about how exosomes are made, what they carry, how they are isolated, and whether they can serve as biomarkers or drug carriers
span.quote: Exosome research is now in its infancy, in-depth understanding of subcellular components and mechanisms involved in exosome formation and specific cell-targeting will bring light on their physiological activities.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Exosomes are constitutively generated from late endosomes, which are formed by inward budding of the limited multivesicular body (MVB) membrane. Invagination of late endosomal membranes results in the formation of intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) within large MVBs [ 15 ]. During this process, certain proteins are incorporated into the invaginating membrane, while the cytosolic components are engulfed and enclosed within the ILVs. Most ILVs are released into the extracellular space upon fusion with the plasma membrane, which are referred to as “exosomes” [ 16 , 17 ]. Alternatively, these components are trafficked to lysosomes for degradation.

span.label: vesicles released when a multivesicular body fuses with the plasma membrane, which cannot be separated in practice from vesicles of other origins in the same size range
span.quote: Exosomes are constitutively generated from late endosomes, which are formed by inward budding of the limited multivesicular body (MVB) membrane. During this process, certain proteins are incorporated into the invaginating membrane, while the cytosolic components are engulfed and enclosed within the ILVs. span.label: narrative review; no new measurement
span.quote: The presence of exosomes in extracellular space was identified as early as in late 1980s [ 1 ]. However, exosomes secreted from cells were initially proposed as cellular waste resulting from cell damage, or by-products of cell homeostasis, and have no significant impact on neighboring cells. It is only recently that these extracellular vesicles are functional vehicles that carry a complex cargo of proteins [ 2 ], lipids [ 3 ], and nucleic aids [ 2 , 4 , 5 ], be capable of delivering these cargos to the target cells they encounter, which may ultimately reprogram the recipient cells distal from their release.

span.label: ONE PAPER, TWO DEFINITIONS OF ITS OWN TITLE WORD. **BY ROUTE**, in the abstract and the biogenesis section: `Exosomes are nano-sized biovesicles released ... UPON FUSION OF MULTIVESICULAR BODIES AND THE PLASMA MEMBRANE`, and `Most ILVs are released into the extracellular space upon fusion with the plasma membrane, WHICH ARE REFERRED TO AS EXOSOMES`. **BY SIZE AND MARKERS**, in Table 1: `Exosome ... Size HOMOLOGOUS 30-100 nm ... Markers ... CD63, TSG101, Alix, flottilin`. The first is a history of the object; the second is a property of it, and only the second can be applied to a tube

span.label: and the biogenesis mechanism the route definition depends on IS ITSELF CONTESTED, which the paper states: `DESPITE THE CONTROVERSY of whether exosome release is an ESCRT-regulated mechanism ...` and `recent evidence favors AN ALTERNATIVE PATHWAY ... in an ESCRT-INDEPENDENT manner`. A class defined by a route whose machinery is under dispute
span.quote: Despite the controversy of whether exosome release is an ESCRT-regulated mechanism, different ESCRT components and ubiquitinated proteins have already been identified in exosomes isolated from various cell types. Additionally, the typical exosomal protein Alix, which is associated with several ESCRT (TSG101 and CHMP4) proteins, has been reported to participate in endosomal membrane budding and abscission, as well as exosomal cargo selection via interaction with syndecan [ 23 ]. These observations led to a hypothesis implicating ESCRT function in exosomal biogenesis.

span.label: THE CLASS WAS WASTE UNTIL RECENTLY: `exosomes secreted from cells were INITIALLY PROPOSED AS CELLULAR WASTE resulting from cell damage, or BY-PRODUCTS of cell homeostasis, and HAVE NO SIGNIFICANT IMPACT on neighboring cells. It is only recently that these extracellular vesicles are functional vehicles`. Same object, same assays, opposite ontological status - the third such history in the corpus after circRNA and microplastics
